text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Finance Minister Viktor Klima is expected to present the winning bid for the government's 70 percent voting stake in Creditanstalt on Saturday after an emergency meeting of the leaders of the divided government coalition.
- Even though the consortium around EA-Generali has improved its bid for Creditanstalt, its offer is believed to be two billion schillings lower than that of rival Bank Austria.

- Creditanstalt reports a 20 percent rise in preliminary 1996 net profit. Chief executive Guido Schmidt-Chiari warns his bank's expansion plans would be in danger should it be taken over by Bank Austria.
- Austria is one of the most expensive countries in the European Union. Only Finland, Denmark, Switzerland, Sweden and Norway are more costly, a study by research institute Nielsen shows.
- Inhabitants of the capital Vienna and the city of Salzburg have the highest purchasing power of all Austrians, Nielsen study shows.
- The 1996/97 winter tourism season got off to a good start, bookings increased particularly over the New Year holidays.
- Austria's electricity providers expect to present Economy a compromise proposal for the reorganisation of the country's energy market to Economy Minister Johannes Farnleitner by the end of January.
DIE PRESSE

- The conservative People's Party and the opposition far-right Freedom Party plan to launch a parliamentary initiative against Bank Austria's bid to take over Creditanstalt by demanding the bank improves its offer to small shareholders.
- Steel maker VA Stahl's chief executive Peter Strahammer says there is no reason to be euphoric about the business outlook for the current year.
- Carton board maker Mayr-Melnhof plans to merge two of its Vienna-based folding carton plants, cutting 120 jobs.
- Austria's National Bank reports a drop in pretax profit to 11.4 billion schillings in 1996 from 12.6 billion a year earlier.
- U.S. carmaker Chrysler may decide whether to build a car parts plant in the souther Austrian city of Graz, near its existing assembly plant, by the end of the month.
KURIER

- The consortium around EA-Generali has substantially improved its offer for Creditanstalt. However, Bank Austria also raised its existing 16.8 billion schillings offer for the state's stake to an alleged 18 billion schillings.
- Tens of thousands of households face a 10 to 15 percent increase in their heating bills because of the unusually cold winter temperatures in recent weeks.
- Steelmaker VA Stahl wants to link up with a strategic partner to brace itself for the concentration process in Europe's steel industry.
- Retailer Spar hopes Austria's extended shopping hours will cause a three to five percent rise in turnover due to longer shop opening hours.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Fibremaker Lenzing expects a loss of 170 million schillings in 1996. The company also expects a loss this year.
- Austria's telecommunications industry will invest some 15 billion schillings this year to improve their network.
